neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The authors explain that zeta's polar term and Dirichlet-character prime correlations cause saturation at total support two, whereas cusp-form coefficient cancellation should preserve diagonal dominance farther than the proved degree-dependent range.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The unit closes the prime-pair computation by summation by parts, then uses its own proof to diagnose the support barrier: for zeta the polar term reaches main scale at total support two, while for cusp forms expected cancellation in shifted coefficient sums should keep the off diagonal small out to that same boundary even though the theorem proves only 2/m.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Distinct matched primes are summed using the Rankin-Selberg estimate sum_{p<=X}|c(p)|^2/p=(1/2)log^2 X+O(log X), producing the r-fold v-integral and completing Theorem 3.1. The following remark analyzes support. For zeta, the explicit-formula polar term has size T^{sum|xi_j|/2} and becomes comparable with T log T at total support two. For a GL(2) cusp form, a pair-correlation off-diagonal is reduced to shifted sums c(m)c(m+h); conjectural square-root cancellation would keep it below the diagonal for |xi_1|+|xi_2|<2, beyond the proved 2/m range.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proof's support condition is audited against two different obstructions: a genuine polar contribution and a technical inability to prove coefficient cancellation. This separates a natural phase boundary from the current method's conservative bound.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Summation by parts turns discrete quadratic prime mass into continuous v weights. The shifted-convolution form of the off diagonal then bridges a support question to a coefficient-cancellation question.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The support-two extension for cusp forms is heuristic, based on square-root cancellation not proved here. The artifact begins but does not complete the subsequent smoothing-removal proof, despite the assignment's emphasis on that topic.
directed.uncertainty: The qualitative boundary diagnosis is explicit; exact support powers and O(T) normalizations are display-dependent.

supported: The artifact completes the matched-prime summation by parts and Theorem 3.1, then explicitly compares the support restriction with zeta's polar term and with conjectural cancellation in shifted cusp-form coefficient sums.
The conclusion that support two is a real zeta boundary but a conjectural farther range for cusp forms is correctly distinguished from the proved 2/m range.
inference: Separating a polar obstruction from a current cancellation bottleneck is a strong conceptual reading.
Calling the shifted convolution a bridge from support to coefficient cancellation is justified by formulas (3.67)-(3.69).

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Spitzer's unique-rotation lemma turns every ordered walk into ordered blocks lying below chords with strictly decreasing slopes; the upper convex envelope makes that decomposition bijective. Counting the block orderings as permutation cycles supplies the factorial subset weights and proves the walk-range identity. Only afterward does the text begin classifying p-adic square-integrable and Rankin-Selberg factors.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For generic increments summing to zero, each ordering has an upper convex envelope whose consecutive blocks lie below their chords and have decreasing slopes. Spitzer's lemma gives a unique cyclic rotation of each block with the first property, while ordering slopes gives the second. This bijects full orderings with set partitions and cyclic orderings of blocks. The maximum M(theta) becomes half the sum of absolute block sums; summing and identifying products (|F_j|-1)! with cycle counts yields the factorial subset formula for T(u), proving Proposition 4.3. The artifact then starts the appendix: p-adic square-integrable representations are segments Delta(n,rho), principal factors reduce to supercuspidal factors, and Rankin-Selberg factors vanish unless twist classes match.
directed.conceptual_reading: A geometric canonicalization—upper convex envelope plus unique rotations—converts maximal deviation into partition combinatorics. On the appendix side, twist classes play an analogous grouping role for deciding which local factors can interact.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Convex-envelope blocks bridge walk maxima to set partitions and permutation-cycle counts. Segment representations Delta(n,rho) bridge p-adic square-integrable data to supercuspidal twist classes.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The walk proof assumes generic increments and extends only by continuity. The p-adic discussion is preliminary and does not yet derive the positive quadratic product or coefficient lower bound described in the assignment metadata.
directed.uncertainty: There is a partial metadata/artifact mismatch: most of the hashed unit proves the Spitzer identity, while only its end starts ramified-factor classification. Exact factorials and local indices are formula-sensitive.

supported: The source uses the upper convex envelope, Spitzer's unique-rotation lemma, decreasing slopes, and a bijection with set partitions and cyclic block orders to prove the walk-range identity.
Only after completing that proof does it begin the p-adic appendix with segment representations, supercuspidal reductions, twist equivalence, and the condition for nontrivial Rankin-Selberg factors.
inference: The convex-envelope blocks genuinely bridge maxima to set partitions and permutation-cycle counts.
Segment representations genuinely bridge square-integrable data to supercuspidal twist classes.

context_or_ocr_risk: The assignment metadata emphasizes ramified positivity, but the hashed unit only begins that analysis; exact factorials and local indices are formula-sensitive.
